Guidewire buys Hyperexponential for $1.7B in cash
items.d: The deal, expected to close sometime next year, is to help bring AI agents to work alongside humans to underwrite, analyze, and price decisions.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 3:26 PM PDT · October 27, 2026 Image Credits: TechCrunch/AI generated Dominic-Madori Davis Guidewire buys Hyperexponential for $1.7B in cash Insurance tech company Guidewire announced Tuesday the acquisition of the agentic underwriting insurance company Hyperexponential for $1.7 billion in cash. The deal, expected to close sometime next year , is to help bring AI agents to work alongside humans to underwrite, analyze, and price decisions. The deal is worth around $2 billion in total, with $400 million in additional capital reserved if certain revenue targets are hit. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz and Battery Ventures, Hyperexponential was founded in 2017 and has raised nearly $90 million to date, according to PitchBook. So this marks a significant return for investors. The U.K.-based AI startup says nearly 600 insurers across 40 different countries use its software. items.t: Bank of America kindly asks that you don’t share your banking password with your AI assistant
items.d: The banking giant reminds customers that "you're responsible for activity" resulting from your AI agents' access.
items.fullText: Financial giant Bank of America is reminding customers to bank safely by kindly not sharing your banking credentials with your AI agent. In an email blast to customers titled “Protecting your finances in the Al World,” Bank of America urged customers to never share their username and password with another person or an outside service, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.” You can practically sense the frustration in the person sending the email. Still, customers are increasingly handing over their log-ins as personal AI assistants grow more popular . Sharing your banking username and password with an AI assistant runs the risk that it could do something with your finances without your knowledge, or that your bank thinks someone’s raiding your account and locks you out of it. Worse, a security flaw in the AI assistant could result in it leaking your banking credentials elsewhere, giving financially motivated hackers a way into your bank account. This latest warning comes as banks are still exploring how AI agents fit into the financial world but are reportedly grappling with unauthorized agents accessing their customers’ money . As we discussed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , banks, payment providers, and processors are still trying to figure out how to allow customers access to their bank accounts using AI tools, such as for agentic payments, which allow people to set agents to autonomously buy things at the best price or the right time. Bank of America did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the email. But heed the bank’s warning, for if things go wrong, it’s on you. Account agreements at most banks hold customers responsible for anyone they give their log-in to. “If you do share your credentials,” its email reads, “keep in mind that you’re responsible for activity resulting from that access.” (via Bryan Toporek ) Topics agentic paym

items.t: Who’s really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO?
items.d: Here's a clear explanation of Anthropic's incredibly complex governance structure.
items.fullText: Anthropic was founded in 2021 to ensure humanity can control AI and benefit from it in the long-term. As the frontier lab approaches its initial public offering, however, there’s one class of humanity that is being shut out of control: anyone who buys its stock on public markets. Complex structures that allow founders like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg to control their public companies without owning most of them are nothing new in Silicon Valley. But Anthropic’s obsession with AI safety has resulted in a truly baroque style of corporate governance that will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions at the AI company, including who sits on its board. First, Anthropic is a public benefit company — a for-profit corporation legally allowed to weigh a public mission alongside profit — with the goal of promoting AI safety. That status protects the board’s ability to make decisions about AI safety that aren’t driven entirely by shareholder value without being sued by angry investors. Right now, the board is chaired by Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and includes CEO Dario Amodei (her brother), Netflix cofounder Reed Hastings, former Microsoft and GM CFO Christopher Liddell, Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, and Spark Capital partner Yasmin Razavi. There is one vacancy on the board. Second, Anthropic has allocated significant control of its board to a Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), an independent panel meant to keep the company focused on mission to benefit humanity. The trust owns a class of stock that gives it the ability to elect and remove a majority of the company’s board, known as Class T directors. The LTBT is chaired by Neil Shah, a global health expert who was managing director at GiveWell, a nonprofit that ranks charities, and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs. items.t: Frontier AI labs say their models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis. What does that mean?
items.d: TechCrunch spoke to the MIT computer scientist charged with explaining OpenAI's latest mind-bending discovery.
items.fullText: OpenAI released solutions to three blockbuster math problems that have long vexed researchers. One was a surprise rejection of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a durable assumption in computer science that plays a large role in how we understand what is difficult to compute. As with previous proof-drops from the frontier lab, scientific communities responded with a mixture of thrill and dismay. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge suggested that OpenAI was basing its solutions on pre-existing work, and hours later, Anthropic subsequently released its own refutation of ETH. However, OpenAI’s process is evolving. This time, the lab structured its releases differently for each of the three disciplines involved: Mathematicians got the work dropped on GitHub; the computer scientists formed a working group, asked for the proofs to be shared publicly and OpenAI to fund a conference to discuss them; the physicists formed a working group that will determine how their result will be released. MIT professor Ryan Williams is the computer scientist who is organizing his field’s response to the new finding. Williams, whose work focuses on these questions of computational complexity, has criticized OpenAI’s approach in the past, calling its proof dump earlier this October a “DDOS attack on mathematicians.” However, he agreed to collaborate with the frontier labs in order to help shepherd ideas that are vital to the field, he told TechCrunch. The lab asked him to help interpret the solution, along with UC San Diego computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published the ETH in 1999. KT가 자체 개발한 ‘오토 모델 라우터’는 질문의 난이도와 요구 품질, 비용을 분석한다. 간단한 요약·번역에는 경량 모델을, 복잡한 추론에는 고성능 모델을 배정하는 방식이다. 입력 문장에서 불필요한 표현을 제거하는 압축 기술도 적용했다. KT에 따르면 프롬프트 압축으로 약 20%, 모델 자동 선택으로 약 5%의 비용 절감 효과를 낸다. 예컨대 ‘다음 주 출장인데 월요일 오전에 서울에서 부산으로 가는 KTX 열차를 찾아줘’라는 질문을 ‘다음 주 월요일 오전 서울 부산 KTX’로 압축하는 식이다. 질문의 의미를 유지하면서 AI가 처리해야 할 토큰 수를 줄여 비용과 응답 시간을 단축한다는 설명이다. 이진형 KT AX사업본부장이 27일 서울 세종로 KT광화문빌딩에서 열린 기자간담회에서 '토큰팩토리' 사업에 대해 발표하고 있다. /사진=KT 제공 토큰팩토리만의 차별점은 국내에서 AI 추론을 직접 수행한다는 것이다. AI 모델 7개는 국내 KT 데이터센터에서 구동된다. 업스테이지 ‘솔라 프로4’, KT ‘믿음 K3.0’, 모티프 ‘모티프3’ 등 국산 모델 3종과 지푸AI의 ‘GLM-5.3-플래시’, 구글 ‘젬마4-31B’ 등 해외 오픈웨이트 모델 4종이다. 오픈웨이트는 모델의 가중치가 공개돼 자체 인프라에서 구동할 수 있는 방식이다. 이진형 KT AX사업본부장은 “해외 모델 제공사와 별도 계약을 맺고 국내 데이터센터에서 직접 추론 서비스를 제공하기로 했다”며 “데이터 처리를 국내에서 수행하는 소버린 AI 환경을 구현하는 데 의미가 있다”고 말했다. 연내 오픈라우터를 입점시켜 글로벌 AI 모델 500개 이상을 확보할 예정이다. 이에 따라 국산 모델, 오픈웨이트

items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic reveals $80 billion loss, huge spending spree ahead of IPO The company warned that AI could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” as cybersecurity fears grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 AI startup Anthropic unveils its public IPO filing for the first time 03:17 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 11:16 AM EDT By Steve Kopack Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic on Monday unveiled its public IPO filing ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest stock debuts in history. That offering, widely expected to come sometime in mid-November, could value the Claude developer at more than $2 trillion. That could surpass the current record holder, Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in an IPO in June that valued the rocket-AI-social-media firm at $2.1 trillion. The filing did not include a potential share price, the number of shares to be offered or a valuation for the whole company, all of which will be determined after Anthropic holds a “road show” with investors, prospective investors and its bankers. Monday’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission showed that Anthropic, like other AI firms, is splashing out unprecedented amounts of cash on cloud services to run its AI models. The company plans to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon for cloud services through April 2036 and another $120 billion with SpaceX through 2029. Anthropic also said it planned to spend $115 billion with Google and $45 billion with Microsoft, both through 2033, for computing infrastructure. The filing said that the company recorded revenue growth of “1,368% year over year for the three months ended June 30, 2026.” The cost of renting servers and chips grew by 300% over the same period. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Elvis Presley’s rights holders sue Anthropic, saying it trained AI on his music Anthropic has said it “disagree[s] with the claims and intend[s] to defend this case fully.” Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Elvis Presley performs in 1955. Michael Ochs Archives / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 25, 2026, 3:11 PM EDT By Angela Yang and Austin Mullen The owners of Elvis Presley’s music have sued Anthropic, alleging it used his copyrighted lyrics without permission to train its AI models and generating infringing versions of his songs. In a lawsuit filed Friday, Authentic Brands Group, the licensing platform that controls Presley’s intellectual property — along with other companies, trusts and individuals who own rights to his music — accused Anthropic of infringing copyrights to 274 songs without any license or payment. These span some of Presley’s biggest hits, including “All Shook Up,” “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “Don’t Be Cruel,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Return to Sender.” “The Elvis Plaintiffs’ iconic collective catalog contains some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history,” the lawsuit stated. The plaintiffs allege that the infringement has occurred throughout “the entire development” of Anthropic’s flagship Claude models and continues today as users generate outputs that reproduce copyrighted lyrics or create unauthorized adaptations of the songs. “As we say in the lawsuit, the Elvis Plaintiffs are guardians of, and highly protective of, Elvis’s song which are some of the most iconic of all time,” attorney Richard Busch wrote in a statement. A spokesperson for Anthropic wrote: “We disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully.” Elvis Presley performs circa 1975. items.fullText: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI.
